accident_role.description: The role the user played in the traffic accident

accident_detail.description: Current status/what the user is doing about the accident

illness_symptom.description: A symptom from the selected illness

family_situation.description: The nature of the family emergency

family_situation_id.description: Internal ID for the family situation (used for gravity)

family_location.description: Where the family emergency is happening

family_situation_update.description: Current status of the family emergency

work_urgency.description: Why the user specifically is needed

work_duration.description: How long the work crisis will take

home_detail.description: Detail about handling the home disaster

car_detail.description: Detail about handling the car trouble

reluctance_signal.description: Signal that the user tried to avoid cancelling

evasion_tactic.description: A way to deflect further questions

minimization.description: A way to downplay the situation

traffic_accident_involved.template_text: {guilt} — {when}, I was at {location} and I was in a {severity}. I'm {detail}. I'm okay, just shaken up. I can't make it tonight.
traffic_accident_involved.believe_notes: Traffic accidents are common but verifiable. Offer location details freely — they check on traffic apps.

traffic_accident_witness.template_text: {guilt}. I witnessed a {severity} at {location} and I need to stay to give a statement. {minimize}. {detail}.
traffic_accident_witness.believe_notes: Witness excuse is noble — implies civic duty. But requires commitment to the bit if questioned.

illness_sudden.template_text: {guilt}. I came down with a {illness} — {symptom}. {unverifiable}. {duration}. I really can't make it.
illness_sudden.believe_notes: Illness is the classic excuse. Don't oversell the symptoms. Vague is better than specific.

illness_severe.template_text: {guilt}. {reluctance}, but I'm really sick. It's a {illness} — {symptom}. I don't think I'll be functional for {duration}.
illness_severe.believe_notes: Severe illness requires commitment. If questioned, don't elaborate beyond what's in the excuse.

family_medical_emergency.template_text: {guilt}. {situation} and I need to be at {location}. {update}. {evasion} — I'll let you know when I know more.
family_medical_emergency.believe_notes: Family emergency is the nuclear option. Use sparingly. The evasion tactic is critical — people generally don't press on family stuff.

work_emergency.template_text: {guilt}. Work thing came up — {crisis} and {urgency}. I know, I know. {reluctance}. Probably {duration}. I'm so sorry.
work_emergency.believe_notes: Work emergency is relatable. Risk: if they know your workplace, they might check. Keep details vague.

home_disaster.template_text: {guilt}. {when}, {disaster}. {detail}. {minimize}, but I really can't leave right now.
home_disaster.believe_notes: Home disaster is hard to verify but also hard to fake details for. Pick a scenario you actually understand.

car_trouble_basic.template_text: {guilt}. My car — {trouble}. {detail}. {minimize}. I'll figure something out for next time.
car_trouble_basic.believe_notes: Car trouble is the safest excuse. Everyone's had it. Don't invent a specific mechanic.

pet_emergency.template_text: {guilt}. My pet is sick and I need to take them to the vet. {detail}. {minimize}.
pet_emergency.believe_notes: Pet emergency is effective because people don't question pet love. Know your vet's name.

vague_personal.believe_notes: Vague and personal. Won't hold up to scrutiny. Best for low-stakes cancellations with people who won't press.

work_then_family.name: Double Whammy
work_then_family.connector: And then, while I was dealing with that,
work_then_family.template_text: {work_text} And then, while I was dealing with that, {family_text}
work_then_family.believe_notes: The double excuse is high risk. It sounds like overkill. Only use if you've established a pattern of reliability.

accident: What does the other car look like?
How long have you been waiting?

Have you been to a doctor?

family_emergency: How long will you be there?
Is there anything I can do?
Have you talked to [your sibling] about this?
work_emergency: Does your boss know you had plans?
Is this the same client as last time?
What happens if you don't go in?
car_trouble: What kind of car do you drive?
How are you getting it fixed?
When's the last time you serviced it?
Can someone give you a ride instead?
general: What do you mean by 'something came up'?
Are you sure you can't make it for even a bit?
This feels like it happens a lot — everything good?
Did you know about this before we made plans?
How are you going to handle it?
Is there anything I can do to help?
Are you being honest with me?

hesitation: That took a second. You sure about that?
Take your time. I want the real answer.
contradiction: Wait — that doesn't match what you said earlier.
You said X before, now you're saying Y. Which is it?
That's a different story than two minutes ago.
I want to believe you, but you're making it hard.
over_explaining: You're giving me a lot of detail. Interesting.
That's very specific for a simple question.
Most people don't remember that much detail. But you do. Convenient.
emotional_deflection: Getting defensive isn't helping your case.
Why are you upset if you're telling the truth?
I'm just asking questions. Your reaction is telling.
If you were honest, this wouldn't bother you.

excellent.comment: Convincing delivery. You either told the truth or you're a sociopath. Either way, they'll buy it.
excellent.advice: You don't need this tool. You need a long look in the mirror.

good.comment: Solid performance. A few rough edges, but nothing that would trigger real suspicion.
good.advice: Stay consistent with the details you committed to. Don't volunteer extra information.

decent.comment: They'll probably believe you, but they'll have doubts. You might get a follow-up text.
decent.advice: Stick to your story. Don't elaborate if they ask again. Silence is your friend.

poor.comment: They know something's up. Maybe not the full truth, but they don't buy your excuse.
poor.advice: Consider partial honesty: 'Okay, it's not exactly what I said, but I really can't make it.'

terrible.comment: That was painful to watch. They absolutely know you're lying.
terrible.advice: Just tell the truth. It's easier. Or get better at this. Your call.
